rv.q: For once, when applied to this mercilessly acute look at the minefield of race in relation to property and language, the term … is not critic-speak for … Norris is very good on the wacky irrationality of racism. … Sophie Thompson tears your heart as his surviving manically cheerful mother, but then all the acting is out of this world. Essential.
Bruce Norris’s provocative 2010 satire hasn’t dated horribly, but feels overwhelmed by the reality of MAGA-era America
It's to the enormous credit of the actors that they almost make us care about them.

cn.t: Bruce Norris's play struggles with underdeveloped characters that feel more like types than fully realized people, though the cast works hard to bring them to life with mixed results.
